b1-31.title: A sports weekend
b1-31.story: Max is a real winter sports [[enthusiast]], so he planned a weekend in the mountains. On Saturday morning, he rented a [[snowboard]] and bought a two-day [[ski pass]]. Anna doesn't like fast sports, so she walked up a forest [[trail]] with Sofia. By lunch, Max had fallen in the snow at least ten times. In the evening, the friends went [[bowling]] at the hotel, and Anna won easily. On Sunday it snowed too much, so they stayed inside. They played [[ping-pong]] in the basement all afternoon. "Next winter," Max laughed, "I'm taking lessons first!"

b1-32.title: Dating and respect
b1-32.story: Anna has a [[crush]] on a boy from her English class, but she is too shy. She asked Ira for some advice about [[dating]]. "Be yourself, and find someone who treats you with [[respect]]," Ira said. That made [[sense]] to Anna. The next day, a doctor gave a health talk at school about love and [[sex]]. She also said that everyone deserves kindness, and that it is okay to be [[gay]]. After class, the boy from English held the door open for Anna. "You're a real [[gentleman]]," she said with a smile. "Only for a real [[lady]]," he answered, and they both laughed. Then they walked home together for the first time.

b1-33.title: A babysitter for my sis
b1-33.story: On Saturday night, Max's parents asked Anna to be a [[babysitter]] for little Sofia. Max stayed home too, but he only wanted to play video games. "Hey [[sis]], what do you want to do?" Anna asked Sofia with a smile. Sofia wanted to visit the [[pet shop]] near their house. There she fell in love with a [[mini]] rabbit, but they couldn't buy it. At home, Sofia drew a white [[pony]] with a long pink tail. Then she covered the whole picture with colorful [[stickers|sticker]]. When her parents came back, Sofia was asleep with the picture in her hands.

b1-34.title: Family game night
b1-34.story: On Friday, Anna's family had a game night at her grandparents' house. Taras is a serious [[gamer]], but Grandma said, "No phones tonight!" First, Grandpa and Dad tried to finish the [[crossword]] in the newspaper. Mama and Anna started a big [[puzzle]] with a picture of Kyiv. Then Grandma brought out her old [[bingo]] cards, and Taras won twice. Later, Taras built a long line on the floor and pushed the first [[domino]]. Mama read everyone's [[horoscope]] from a magazine, and Grandpa laughed at his. At the end, Grandma opened the [[photo album]] and showed them Dad as a little boy. "This is better than my phone!" Taras said.

b1-35.title: At a rock festival
b1-35.story: Last summer, Max and Lisa camped for three days at a [[rock festival]]. Lisa had never been to a [[live concert]] before, so she was very excited. On the first night, they saw a [[rock band]] from Kharkiv on the main stage. The [[drummer]] counted to four, and the whole crowd started jumping. Then the [[guitarist]] played a solo that lasted almost five minutes. On the second day, a young [[rapper]] surprised everyone by joining the band. Max called his dad, who loves old [[rock and roll]], and held up his phone. Now Max and Lisa are saving money for a [[rock concert]] in Kyiv.

b1-36.title: A summer jazz festival
b1-36.story: Every summer, Anna's family goes to the [[jazz festival]] in the park. Dad has loved [[jazz]] since he was a teenager. The bands come on stage at thirty-minute [[intervals|interval]]. This year, the first musician played the [[saxophone]] so beautifully that Mama closed her eyes. Then an old [[pianist]] played a slow [[waltz]], and Grandpa danced with Grandma. Taras liked a children's band best, because one girl played the [[xylophone]]. Next came a group that mixed [[folk]] songs with modern sounds. Between two bands, Anna met a music [[producer]] who was buying coffee. Before he could say a word, Taras ran up and said, "I can play the drums!"

b1-37.title: Old films and poems
b1-37.story: Anna's grandpa found an old [[disc]] in a box and put it into the DVD player. It was a film about a young [[poet]] from the [[era]] of black-and-white TV. Grandpa said that a [[critic]] once called his poems "too funny." But Grandpa has always loved their gentle [[humor]]. His favorite poem was about a [[phoenix]] that rises from its own ashes. Luckily, he still had all the poems on an old computer [[disk]]. Anna's mama, who works as a [[designer]], decided to make a small book of them. On Grandpa's birthday, she gave him the book with a bright red bird on the cover.

b1-38.title: English grammar class
b1-38.story: In English class on Monday, Anna's teacher started with word building. First, she explained that the [[prefix]] "un" in "unhappy" means "not." Then the class added the [[suffix]] "-ness" to "kind" and made "kindness." Max had to find an [[antonym]] for "hot," and he quickly said "cold." Next, they learned that "to swim" is an [[infinitive]]. In her short letter, Ira forgot to put a [[comma]] after "Dear Lisa." The teacher also reminded everyone that B is a [[consonant]] and A is a vowel. Then Anna and Max practiced a short [[dialogue]] about ordering food in a café. Max tried to speak with a British [[accent]], and the whole class laughed. For homework, they had to do exercise six in their [[workbook]].
